title: IELTS Advanced CEFR-J comparison
scopeNote: The task brief named 694 terms; the file contained 777 distinct terms when reviewed, so the comparison covers all 777 present at that time.

source.name: CEFR-J Wordlist Version 1.6
source.compiler: Yukio Tono, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies
source.citation: The CEFR-J Wordlist Version 1.6. Compiled by Yukio Tono, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies. Retrieved from https://www.cefr-j.org/download.html on 2026-11-18.
source.rights: The source page identifies Tono Laboratory at TUFS as copyright holder and permits research and commercial use with proper acknowledgement.
source.coverage: The published vocabulary levels cover A1 through B2, with headwords and parts of speech. The source describes its list as textbook-corpus-based and notes it may contain errors.

method.matching: Compared case-insensitive exact headwords and the course entry's part of speech against the CEFR-J v1.6 ALL sheet. No inflection, spelling, or phrase-component matching was used.
method.reassignment: Exact headword-and-part-of-speech matches reported at A1–B2 were moved to the standard IELTS course. A headword match with a different part of speech was not assigned that source level and remains in IELTS Advanced.
method.limits: CEFR-J v1.6 stops at B2. A missing or part-of-speech-mismatched entry does not establish C1 or C2 and receives no CEFR label.
method.labels: Levels in sourceLevel reproduce the CEFR-J source entry only; they are not presented as an official CEFR certification for the learner or the course.
